Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to

SPECIFICATION FOR 
BRAIDED TAPE FOR BERETS 



(Reaffirmed 2002) 



1. Scope — Covers braided tape for berets made from viscose-rayon-spun staple yarn. 

2. Manufacture 

2,i Yarn — 16 fl ( or 37 tex ) spun from viscose rayon cut staple. 

2.2 Braided Tape — Flat braided on 16 spindle machine with 3 ends working as one under even 
tension, with uniform and firm selvedges, and free from all braiding defects. 

2.2.1 It shall be free from sizing, filling and dressing materials and from substances liable to cause 
subsequent tendering. 

2.2.2 It shall normally be dyed black and the dyeing should be free from stains, streaks, etc. 

2.2.3 Sulphur dyes shall not be used. 

3. Requirements — See Tables 1 and 2.

IS: 8302- 1977 

4. Make-Up and Packing — Tapes shall be made into light rolls. The rolls shall be arranged in 
cylindrical bundles and shall be secured by twine of adequate strength. These bundles shall be 
wrapped in 2 layers of kraft paper [See IS : 1397-1967 Specification for kraft paper ( first revision ) ] 
followed by a third layer of waterproof packing paper (see IS: 1398-1968 Specification for packing paper, 
waterproof, bitumen laminated ) and finally with an outer layer of cloth heavy cee ( see IS : 3751-1966 
Specification for heavy cee cloth ) to form a bale. 

5. Marking 

5.1 Each roll shall be marked with the following: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of the manufacturer, initials or trade-mark, if any; 

c) Length of tape in the roll ( m) and width (mm); 

d) Year of manufacture. 

5.2 ISI Certification Marking — Optional; details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This Standard covers the requirements of braided tape given in INO/TC/4052 Berets, knitted; 
one-piece, Issued by Ministry of Defence, Government of India.
